newsitem.title: CHILE: Scores trapped by snow at Chile-Argentine border.
newsitem.headline: Scores trapped by snow at Chile-Argentine border.

text.p: Over 200 people have been trapped by a blizzard for over 24 hours at two border stations high in the Andes on the Argentine-Chilean frontier, with all roads to them cut by over four feet (1.3 metres) of snow, police said on Friday.
Authorities were trying to clear roads with snowplows but officials might have to rescue the people by helicopter when the storm clears -- not expected until Sunday, officials said.

A total of 127 people, 15 of them children, were trapped at the immigration office in the Los Libertadores pass, the main land crossing between the two nations, as the buses, trucks and cars they were travelling in were forced to stop by snow.
About 70 other people were isolated in a nearby customs station and waiting for help to arrive after the blizzard blew in on Thursday, authorities said.

"There is enough food for them all for a week. Weather conditions are preventing us from reaching them and we are looking at the possibility of reaching them by air when the weather improves," said police spokesman Gonzalo Cienfuegos on local television.

The travellers have been trapped at the two stations, both of the Chilean side of the border, since Thursday afternoon when the storm blew in off the Pacific, dumping heavy rain on central Chile and snow at higher elevations.

The buildings were the travellers are trapped are large, metal structures with few comforts but ample space, a few miles (kilometres) up the road from the Portillo ski resort. The Chilean Andes have had unusually heavy snowfalls so far this winter after below-normal levels in the past few years.
